key_insight: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization (GGPO) removes learner-to-behavior importance weights by optimizing a KL-adjusted log-mean-exp gap over grouped responses, yielding a stable off-policy objective for verifiable-reward RL.
engineering_relevance: For language-model RL pipelines with stale or offline data, GGPO offers a practical way to train against policy mismatch while controlling variance and preserving reward gains.
method: Minimize a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards across multiple responses to the same prompt.
Derive the objective from KL-regularized policy optimization so the population loss matches the KL-regularized optimality gap on-policy.
Use reference refresh analysis and local reference control to bound final-policy reward under policy staleness and finite data.
evidence_signal: In experiments on mathematical reasoning, GGPO outperformed GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch and fixed offline data, and a default refresh schedule scored 46.58 versus 32.96 with a fixed reference on the five-benchmark weighted average.
watch_item: Performance depends on reference refresh and coverage assumptions, so stale references or poor prompt-response coverage can weaken the bound and degrade results.
paper_title: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards
